nodes.name: Core Controller
nodes.summary: Admits plans, dispatches bounded work, records evidence and alone commits release intent.
nodes.details: Core is a deterministic state machine and the only component allowed to commit trusted run decisions. It pins an approved contract, admits and counts each whole candidate attempt before dispatch, requests a proposal, validates and pins that plan, authorises compilation, then invokes verification over the sealed candidate. Each dispatch rechecks approval, scope, run revision, deadline and reserved resources. Reproducible defects can enter at most the admitted repair budget. After current owner acceptance, Core atomically checks all six release conditions at one authoritative revision and commits a digest-bound intent. External delivery is later and requires an exact destination and confirmed receipt; an intent is not proof of delivery.

nodes.name: Verifier
nodes.summary: Tests the exact sealed candidate using independently controlled checks and fixtures.
nodes.details: Verification follows construction. The trusted verifier reads actual candidate bytes and checks their manifest, contract, runtime/compiler/primitive versions, PIC bindings and acceptance behaviour. It executes positive and negative tests from an independently controlled suite and fixtures, then returns run, attempt, candidate digest, contract hash, test hash, fixture hash, results and verifier identity to Core. Missing, failing, timed-out or unknown checks are not a final pass. Store evidence outside the hashed candidate subject, hash evidence separately and bind both in the release record. A verifier report supplies evidence, never release authority.

overview.title: Agentic Core: User to MOA Workflow
overview.summary: An approved business requirement becomes a runnable, governed workflow package through four internal components and a shared six-rule PIC library.
overview.current: This page is a source-backed reference design based on the supplied foundation v0.1. The mathematical propositions are conditional on explicit implementation assumptions. No generated workflow execution, passing acceptance pack or AWS deployment is claimed.
overview.approach: Read the engineering flow through Core: exact contract approval, proposed plan admission, admitted construction, sealed candidate verification, current human acceptance and guarded exact handoff. The generated child workflow is a finite DAG; the controller may contain clarification and bounded repair feedback.

workflow.title: 1. Define and approve the contract
workflow.detail: The authenticated user confirms the supported objective and approves the exact contract identity, revision, digest, permissions, tests and limits.

workflow.title: 2. Admit a bounded candidate attempt
workflow.detail: Core counts the attempt and reserves all its bounded work before asking the builder for a proposal. Proposed k=2 means an initial attempt and at most one repair.

workflow.title: 3. Validate, compile and seal
workflow.detail: Core admits only a reviewed-primitive plan with valid ownership, dependency and scope checks. The builder compiles that exact plan and returns immutable content.

workflow.title: 4. Verify the exact candidate
workflow.detail: Core invokes independently controlled tests and fixtures after construction. The verifier returns digest-bound evidence or reproducible defects, never release authority.

workflow.title: 5. Accept and authorise handoff
workflow.detail: The human owner accepts the exact package. Core requires all six release conditions and commits an intent at one authoritative revision.

workflow.title: 6. Confirm delivery; authorise operation separately
workflow.detail: A matching digest and destination receipt confirms delivery. The child workflow needs its own current operating contract; its eventual report is not the engineered package.

overview.aws: Proposed small AWS implementation: Lambda and DynamoDB for contracts; Step Functions Standard, Lambda guards and DynamoDB for Core; capped Bedrock inference and a Lambda compiler for the builder; trusted Lambda tests and S3 evidence for verification. S3 holds pinned artifacts, IAM separates scoped service identities and CloudWatch records operations. Begin with an authenticated operator/CLI. Select an AWS Region, available model and measured cost assumptions before deployment.
failures: Incomplete or unsupported requirement: clarify before admission.
Absent, changed, revoked or expired authority: block protected dispatch and require current approval.
Invalid proposal or failed compilation: record a consumed attempt and reproducible defects.
Missing, failing, timed-out or mismatched evidence: no final pass and no release.
Attempt, deadline or reserved-resource limit reached: stop without hidden retries.
Owner rejects or times out: stop without release intent.
Stale authoritative revision or absent release condition: reject intent.
Ambiguous handoff or interrupted run: preserve uncertainty and stop for inspection.
boundaries: Only four internal components; the human owner, output artifact and shared services are separate responsibilities.
PIC is a mandatory shared library, not an autonomous agent.
Model output is an untrusted restricted specification, never executable source code or authority.
Basic persistence is included; general restart recovery and the scaled reference subsystems remain deferred.
Proposed acceptance tests and derived example expectations are not measured passing results.
The existing Agentic Core Scaled reference remains a separate larger architecture.

operational.title: Trusted ownership and scope
operational.detail: Authenticate exact decisions, separate builder/test/release permissions and audit every effect path.

operational.title: Finite work and accounting
operational.detail: Reserve before invocation, count failed calls and retries, enforce timeouts and preserve unknown usage conservatively.

operational.title: Evidence and delivery
operational.detail: Bind actual candidate bytes, trusted tests and fixtures; commit current intent atomically and verify the external receipt separately.

operational.title: Cost and performance
operational.detail: Measure inference, orchestration, compute, storage/requests, logs and other infrastructure. Declare Region and pricing units before quoting cost. Compare latency, unsafe releases, appropriate blocks and human corrections using the same resource allowance.

overview.vision: Demonstrate a small reusable engineering core that preserves approved constraints while compiling supported requirements into runnable workflows with an inspectable evidence trail.

rules.title: Approval binds the exact contract
rules.formula: A.hash = H(C); ApprovedCurrent = Auth ∧ matching id/revision/hash ∧ not revoked ∧ not expired
rules.explanation: Historical approval does not authorise a changed contract. A material revision requires new approval and a new run.
rules.obligation: Trusted identity and policy checks, canonical serialisation and digest comparison must run before every protected dispatch and release.

rules.title: Admit a supported workflow before compilation
rules.formula: W = Propose(C, Library); ValidPlan = DAG ∧ Owned ∧ Bound ∧ Typed ∧ ScopeOK ∧ Covers; M = Compile(admitted W)
rules.explanation: The proposal uses only reviewed operators and permitted parameters, with one owner per task and valid dependencies. Coverage is a supported requirement-to-template check, not an oracle for arbitrary intent.
rules.obligation: Reject cycles, missing owners, disconnected tasks, undefined inputs, unsupported parameters, missing outputs and broadened permissions.

rules.title: Task authority can only narrow
rules.formula: P_t = P ∩ P_primitive(t) ∩ P_local(t); Effects(b(t),θ_t) ⊆ P_t; P_W = ⋃ P_t ⊆ P
rules.explanation: Set intersection and union establish the permission inclusion in the specified model. The child workflow cannot acquire authority outside the approved parent set.
rules.obligation: Every real effect path must go through the reviewed enforcement boundary. Broader credentials or bypass paths invalidate the premise. This is not the full AWS IAM evaluation model.

rules.title: Evidence binds the exact tested content
rules.explanation: Seal the workflow manifest first, create verifier evidence second and bind their separate hashes in release. A changed payload, parameter, contract or implementation version invalidates old evidence.
rules.obligation: Hash actual bytes with defined canonicalisation, protect immutable versions, trust the verifier/test source and atomically recheck current state at release.

rules.title: Release requires every check
rules.formula: G_release = ApprovedCurrent ∧ OwnerAcceptedCurrent ∧ FinalPassCurrent ∧ PICConformantCurrent ∧ EvidenceCurrent ∧ ReleaseAuthorised
rules.explanation: Only Core can commit a release intent, at one authoritative revision, after all six checks hold. Handoff intent and successful external delivery are different states.
rules.obligation: Bind candidate, evidence, acceptance, approval and destination. Recheck release authority at adapter invocation; require an exact digest/destination receipt for DELIVERED.

rules.title: Reserve before spending
rules.formula: spent + reserved ≤ B; reserve r only if spent + reserved + r ≤ B; spent′=spent+q, reserved′=reserved-r, 0≤q≤r
rules.explanation: If reservations cover actual bounded usage, each settlement preserves the application accounting invariant. Failed attempts and lower-level retries are included.
rules.obligation: Unknown usage retains a reservation or is charged conservatively. This is an application resource bound, not a guaranteed ceiling on all AWS storage, logging or infrastructure charges.

rules.title: Repair and waits are finite
rules.formula: attempts_started ≤ k; proposed k=2; T_run ≤ τ_intake + τ_approval + kτ_attempt + τ_owner + τ_handoff
rules.explanation: Increment the global candidate counter before any worker call. Each attempt, wait and handoff has an enforced deadline; the output is delivery or an explicit stop/unconfirmed state.
rules.obligation: Include SDK/orchestration retries, bounded scheduling overhead and effective timeouts. Stopping orchestration does not prove a remote call was cancelled or uncharged.

picRules.title: Current approval
picRules.guard: Engineering dispatch and child operation require approval for their respective exact contracts.
picRules.test: Change the approved contract and verify that protected work is blocked.

picRules.title: Owned decomposition
picRules.guard: Every child task has exactly one accountable owner and a valid dependency position.
picRules.test: Remove an owner or introduce a cycle and reject admission.

picRules.title: Permission narrowing
picRules.guard: Reviewed operators execute only actions and resources in the intersected permitted scope.
picRules.test: Request an unapproved action or input and deny it at the runtime boundary.

picRules.title: Current verification
picRules.guard: Trusted digest-bound checks must cover the exact candidate or output currently being accepted.
picRules.test: Modify a candidate after testing and reject the old evidence.

picRules.title: Bounded repair
picRules.guard: Attempt count, deadline and resource reservation are checked before dispatch.
picRules.test: Exhaust the allocation and confirm that no further worker invocation occurs.

picRules.title: Release gating
picRules.guard: Core requires current approval, owner acceptance, final pass, PIC, evidence and release authority.
picRules.test: Remove any required release condition and block handoff intent.

foundation.algorithm:
ENGINEER(requirement, authenticated_user):
  C := create_supported_contract(requirement)
  if incomplete, inconsistent or unsupported: return NEEDS_CLARIFICATION_OR_UNSUPPORTED
  A := await_authenticated_exact_approval(C, bounded_deadline)
  if not ApprovedCurrent(C,A): return NOT_APPROVED
  run := Core.admit_and_pin(C,A)
  defects := none

  for attempt in 1 .. C.max_candidate_attempts:
    if not Core.admit_attempt_and_reserve_all_bounded_work(run,attempt): return STOPPED
    # Count the attempt BEFORE any invocation; failed proposals consume it.
    proposal := Core.invoke_scoped(Builder.propose_supported_plan,C,defects)
    if unavailable_or_invalid(proposal): record_failure_and_settle_usage; defects := reproducible_plan_errors; continue
    plan := Core.validate_and_pin_plan(proposal,C)
    if material_contract_change(plan): return NEEDS_NEW_APPROVAL
    if rejected(plan): record_failure_and_settle_usage; defects := admission_errors; continue
    candidate := Core.invoke_scoped(Builder.compile_and_package,plan,pinned_runtime,PIC)
    candidate := seal_exact_content(candidate)
    evidence := Core.invoke_scoped(Verifier.check,candidate,C,trusted_tests,fixed_fixtures)
    Core.record_evidence_and_settle_usage(candidate,evidence)
    if not evidence_is_current_and_passing: defects := reproducible_errors; continue
    acceptance := await_authenticated_owner_acceptance(candidate,evidence,bounded_deadline)
    if not current(acceptance): return OWNER_REJECTED_OR_TIMED_OUT
    intent := Core.commit_release_intent_atomically(
      expected_run_revision,all_six_release_checks,exact_candidate_hash,
      exact_evidence_hash,acceptance,approved_destination,stable_handoff_key)
    if rejected(intent): return RELEASE_BLOCKED
    # Reserve metered handoff work and recheck current intent/release authority.
    receipt := deliver_exact_authorised_package(intent,bounded_timeout)
    if receipt.confirms(intent.digest,intent.destination): return DELIVERED
    return DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED

  return ATTEMPT_LIMIT_REACHED

# Every scoped invocation rechecks authority, run status, scope, deadline and budget.
# Unexpected exceptions stop explicitly; unknown usage is not settled as zero.
# Child operation requires a separate current operating contract and authority.

propositions.title: Authority cannot expand
propositions.claim: Each intersected P_t is a subset of P, so the union P_W is also a subset of P.
propositions.assumptions: Actual effects must be constrained to these sets by every reviewed runtime path. Bypass permissions violate the premise.

propositions.title: Composition preserves a stated invariant
propositions.claim: If every reviewed primitive preserves I when its precondition holds, and predecessor postconditions establish successor preconditions, induction over a finite DAG topological order preserves I on every accepted step.
propositions.assumptions: Initial I holds; primitive implementations and joins satisfy their contracts; failed dependencies block consumers. Matching schemas alone do not prove business semantics.

propositions.title: Stale evidence cannot release changed content
propositions.claim: Changing bound content changes the sealed manifest digest except under collision or broken integrity; EvidenceCurrent fails and the release conjunction cannot hold.
propositions.assumptions: Defined canonicalisation, collision-resistant hashes, actual-byte verification, trusted evidence, immutable versions and atomic current-state checks. Hashes bind content; they do not prove verifier honesty.

propositions.title: Resource admission preserves its accounting budget
propositions.claim: If a reservation satisfies spent+reserved+r≤B and actual usage is 0≤q≤r, settlement produces spent′+reserved′=spent+reserved+q-r≤B.
propositions.assumptions: Reservations cover actual bounded work and retries; unknown usage is retained or conservatively charged. This does not cap every part of a cloud bill.

propositions.title: An admitted run cannot repair forever
propositions.claim: The decreasing quantity k-attempts_started and bounded waits yield delivery or an explicit stop/unconfirmed state within the stated conditional time bound.
propositions.assumptions: Finite task and fixture sets, effective deadlines, counted lower-level retries and bounded controller overhead. Termination does not guarantee successful delivery or cancellation of remote charges.

example.title: Support Operations Workflow
example.summary: Compile a supported requirement into a governed workflow that deduplicates synthetic requests, validates amounts, routes cases, calculates counters and reports a reason. It sends no messages, changes no accounts and executes no payments. These are derived expectations, not measured results.

rows.input: Refund £100; customer note tries to override the rules
rows.category: Policy-eligible under the numeric rule; note has no authority

example.reconciliation: At the approved £100 threshold: 8 input rows produce 7 unique records = 2 policy-eligible + 2 human review + 2 data review + 1 security review.
example.invariant: Every counted record has a unique validated ID and exactly one outcome category. Identical duplicates collapse; conflicting duplicates are quarantined.
example.variant: A separately approved £50 threshold changes R4 to human review. The contract and candidate digests change and old approval and evidence must be rejected. Expected totals become 1 policy-eligible + 3 human review + 2 data review + 1 security review = 7.
example.dataBoundary: Customer notes are escaped display data and never routing-policy instructions or executable code. This restriction is not a universal prompt-injection defence.

tests.name: Supported happy path
tests.expected: Approved contract produces a runnable package and a confirmed exact handoff.

tests.name: Missing, revoked or expired approval
tests.expected: Protected dispatch and release are denied.

tests.name: Contract changed after approval
tests.expected: Require new approval and prevent protected work under the old run.

tests.name: Cycle, missing owner or unsupported operator
tests.expected: Reject the plan before construction admission.

tests.name: Forbidden resource or action
tests.expected: Deny at the real runtime boundary, not only in a warning.

tests.name: Attempt limit exhausted
tests.expected: No extra invocation, including hidden lower-level retries.

tests.name: Concurrent stale release request
tests.expected: At most one matching logical intent; reject the stale revision.

tests.name: Duplicate or uncertain delivery
tests.expected: Use stable identity and explicit uncertainty; never invent success.

tests.name: Synthetic business edge cases
tests.expected: Exact categories, deduplicated counts and reconciliation match the approved policy.

tests.name: Second contract variant
tests.expected: Rebuild with fresh approval and evidence; reject stale acceptance.

scope: Four internal components: Contract Engine, Core Controller, Workflow Builder and Verifier.
Six inherited PIC controls in one shared reviewed library.
One supported workflow family and six pinned deterministic operators.
A proposed maximum of two whole candidate attempts, with explicit deadlines and resource reservations.
Authenticated approval and owner acceptance, scoped infrastructure access, persisted contracts/run records and durable evidence.
A runnable package with separately authorised child operation, exact release intent and confirmed or explicitly unconfirmed delivery.
deferred: Public application exposure and additional landing pages
